headerBody: Spain: Tourist Scams documents 103 specific scams against Spanish police and consumer-agency sources — the Policía Nacional (091), Guardia Civil (062), OMIC municipal consumer offices and FACUA — plus r/SpainTravel reports and verified Spanish news. The exact scripts, the tells that give them away, and the Spanish phrases that shut them down. Not a recycled blog list.
quadHead: Four ways Spain catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: Barajas Airport Taxi Overcharge
quad.tl: A run that should cost the posted €33 flat rate inside the M-30 ticks up to €60–€110 — “broken meter,” “luggage fee,” “M-40 routing.” Demand the €33 rate before the bags go in the boot.

quad.title: The Bird-Poop Splash
quad.tl: Something wet hits your shoulder near La Rambla; a “helpful” stranger appears within seconds with tissues while an accomplice empties your bag. The “bird poop” is mustard squirted from a hidden bottle.

quad.title: Three-Card Monte Shell Game
quad.tl: A fake winning crowd at Plaza de España pulls you in; the ball is always palmed, so €20+ bets vanish in seconds — and a “police officer” confederate shows up to extort an “illegal gambling fine” if you object.

quad.title: The Tourist-Trap Paella
quad.tl: Beachfront and tourist-strip kitchens plate frozen-and-microwaved paella at €30 per person, “minimum two,” plus €3–€5 cover and a terrace supplement never mentioned at seating — against €15–€18 in residential Ruzafa.

body: Spain: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Spanish police and consumer-agency sources — the Policía Nacional (091), the Guardia Civil (062), OMIC municipal consumer offices and FACUA — plus r/SpainTravel reports and verified Spanish news. Sourced, not recycled.

103 specific scams across Barcelona, Madrid, Seville, Granada, Valencia and 11 more cities. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Spanish phrases that shut them down — in plain Spanish you can show on your phone, with the steps to file a denuncia if it has already happened.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched and updated every year — the current edition lives in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Spain relaxed, not braced.
